claim: Oligodendrocytes (OLs) are the myelin-forming CNS glia.
source: Oligodendrocytes (OLs), the myelin-forming CNS glia, are highly vulnerable to cellular stresses, and a severe myelin loss underlies numerous CNS disorders.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as an established fact about oligodendrocytes.

claim: Oligodendrocytes are highly vulnerable to cellular stresses.
source: Oligodendrocytes (OLs), the myelin-forming CNS glia, are highly vulnerable to cellular stresses, and a severe myelin loss underlies numerous CNS disorders.
evidence: This is stated as an established characteristic of oligodendrocytes in the abstract.

claim: Severe myelin loss underlies numerous CNS disorders.
source: Oligodendrocytes (OLs), the myelin-forming CNS glia, are highly vulnerable to cellular stresses, and a severe myelin loss underlies numerous CNS disorders.
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge in the abstract.

claim: Adult OL progenitors (OPCs) are the primary players for OL regeneration.
source: Although adult OL progenitors (OPCs) are the primary players for OL regeneration, targetable OPC-specific intracellular signaling mechanisms for facilitated OL regeneration remain elusive.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: OPC-targeted PTEN inactivation markedly promotes OL differentiation and regeneration in the mature CNS.
source: Here, we report that OPC-targeted PTEN inactivation in the mouse, in contrast to OL-specific manipulations, markedly promotes OL differentiation and regeneration in the mature CNS.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the abstract and supported by multiple experiments throughout the manuscript.

claim: Additional deletion of mTOR did not reverse the enhanced OL development from PTEN-deficient OPCs.
source: Unexpectedly, an additional deletion of mTOR did not reverse the enhanced OL development from PTEN-deficient OPCs.
evidence: This is a key finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated experimentally in the results section.

claim: Ablation of GSK3β enhanced OL development.
source: Instead, ablation of GSK3β, another downstream signaling molecule that is negatively regulated by PTEN-Akt, enhanced OL development.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in the results section.

claim: PTEN persistently suppresses OL development in an mTOR-independent manner.
source: Our results suggest that PTEN persistently suppresses OL development in an mTOR-independent manner, and at least in part, via controlling GSK3β activity.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study stated in the abstract, based on the experimental findings.

claim: PTEN suppresses OL development at least in part via controlling GSK3β activity.
source: Our results suggest that PTEN persistently suppresses OL development in an mTOR-independent manner, and at least in part, via controlling GSK3β activity.
evidence: This is a mechanistic conclusion stated in the abstract based on experimental data.

claim: NG2 and PDGFRα-expressing OPCs are abundant throughout life in the mammalian CNS.
source: In the mammalian central nervous system (CNS), NG2 and PDGFRα (platelet-derived growth factor receptor α)-expressing OPCs (also known as NG2+ cells) are abundant throughout life (Dimou and Gallo, 2015; Nishiyama et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: The lineage progression from OPC to OL is a multi-step process involving gradual changes in cell morphology and properties.
source: The lineage progression from OPC to OL is a multi-step process that involves gradual changes in cell morphology and properties, from OPCs to pre-myelinating OLs (pre-OLs) to fully mature OLs, culminating in the formation of lipid-rich myelin around axons (myelinogenesis) (Nave and Werner, 2014).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: In the adult CNS, OPCs continue to serve as the primary reservoir for homeostatic maintenance of OLs by generating new myelinating OLs in the event of OL loss.
source: In the adult CNS, OPCs continue to serve as the primary reservoir for homeostatic maintenance of OLs by generating new myelinating OLs in the event of OL loss (Chamberlain et al., 2016; Young et al., 2013), while they proliferate and sustain their own population size (Hughes et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: OPCs proliferate and sustain their own population size.
source: In the adult CNS, OPCs continue to serve as the primary reservoir for homeostatic maintenance of OLs by generating new myelinating OLs in the event of OL loss (Chamberlain et al., 2016; Young et al., 2013), while they proliferate and sustain their own population size (Hughes et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: Genetic ablation of proposed OL development regulators often resulted in only transient delay in early myelination.
source: Indeed, genetic ablation of proposed OL development regulators often resulted in only transient delay in early myelination (He et al., 2017; Huang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as a general observation from previous studies with supporting citations.

claim: There are far fewer examples of significantly improved OL generation and regeneration in the mature CNS compared to molecules whose loss-of-function results in myelin defects.
source: Moreover, in contrast to a plethora of molecules whose loss-of-function results in myelin defects, there are far fewer examples of significantly improved OL generation and regeneration in the mature CNS.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in the field based on the literature.

claim: mTOR signaling is necessary for proper CNS myelination in early life.
source: The mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) signaling is known to be necessary for proper CNS myelination in early life (Figlia et al., 2018; Lebrun-Julien et al., 2014; Wahl et al., 2014; Wood et al., 2013), but the therapeutic potential of mTOR signaling manipulation for improved OL regeneration is not clear (Jiang et al., 2016; Lebrun-Julien et al., 2014; McLane et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: The therapeutic potential of mTOR signaling manipulation for improved OL regeneration is not clear.
source: The mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) signaling is known to be necessary for proper CNS myelination in early life (Figlia et al., 2018; Lebrun-Julien et al., 2014; Wahl et al., 2014; Wood et al., 2013), but the therapeutic potential of mTOR signaling manipulation for improved OL regeneration is not clear (Jiang et al., 2016; Lebrun-Julien et al., 2014; McLane et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as an unresolved question in the field with supporting citations.

claim: TSC1 and PTEN are negative regulators of mTORC1 activity.
source: As an effort to identify OPC-intrinsic signaling mechanisms that promote OL generation in the mature CNS, we first determined whether the OPC-specific increase in mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1) activity enhances OL development, by OPC-specific genetic deletion of the tuberous sclerosis complex 1 (TSC1) or phosphatase and tensin homolog (PTEN), the two negative regulators of mTORC1 activity (see Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1A showing the signaling pathway.

claim: OPC-targeted PTEN inactivation remarkably facilitates OL regeneration and promotes remyelination after toxin-induced demyelination.
source: OPC-targeted PTEN inactivation also remarkably facilitates OL regeneration and promotes remyelination after toxin-induced demyelination.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the introduction and supported by experimental data in the results section.

claim: OL-specific PTEN ablation did not show positive outcomes observed with OPC-specific PTEN ablation.
source: However, such positive outcomes were not observed for OL-specific PTEN ablation.
evidence: This is a key finding stated in the introduction and demonstrated experimentally in the results section.

claim: OPC-specific TSC1 inactivation impaired OL development/survival.
source: Moreover, in contrast to PTEN, OPC-specific TSC1 inactivation impaired OL development/survival.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the introduction and supported by experimental data in the results section.

claim: Three 4HT injections (1 mg per injection) were given between P20 and P21 to Pdgfra-CreER; R26-EYFP; ±Tsc1f/f mice.
source: Three 4HT injections (1 mg per injection) were given between P20 and P21 (a total of 3 mg of 4HT).
evidence: This experimental detail is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: There was a significant increase in the percentage of pS6 immunopositive cells among all callosal EYFP+ cells in Pdgfra-CreER; R26-EYFP; Tsc1f/f mice at P20+21.
source: Three weeks after the first 4HT injection (P20 +21), there was a significant increase in the percentage of phosphorylated S6 ribosomal protein (pS6) immunopositive cells among all callosal EYFP+ cells in Pdgfra-CreER; R26-EYFP; Tsc1f/f mice (p=0.042) (Figure 1C,D), indicating that mTORC1 activity is enhanced (Hara et al., 1998) as a result of effective TSC1 inactivation.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text with statistical significance and supported by Figure 1C,D showing the data.

claim: The increase in pS6 immunopositive cells indicates that mTORC1 activity is enhanced as a result of effective TSC1 inactivation.
source: Three weeks after the first 4HT injection (P20 +21), there was a significant increase in the percentage of phosphorylated S6 ribosomal protein (pS6) immunopositive cells among all callosal EYFP+ cells in Pdgfra-CreER; R26-EYFP; Tsc1f/f mice (p=0.042) (Figure 1C,D), indicating that mTORC1 activity is enhanced (Hara et al., 1998) as a result of effective TSC1 inactivation.
evidence: This interpretation is stated in the text with a supporting citation and demonstrated by the data in Figure 1C,D.

claim: The number of EYFP+ cells was remarkably reduced in Tsc1 cKO mice, particularly in the CC.
source: However, to our surprise, the number of EYFP+ cells was remarkably reduced in Tsc1 cKO mice, particularly in the CC (Figure 1E,F).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1E,F showing the data.

claim: The number of newly generated OLs (EYFP+CC1+) was severely reduced in both the CC and CTX of Tsc1 cKO mice at P20+21.
source: Co-immunostaining with antibodies against OL lineage stage markers (i.e. NG2 and CC1) (Figure 1E) revealed that the number of newly generated OLs (EYFP+CC1+) was severely reduced, both in the CC (p=0.016) and CTX (p=0.0007) of the cKO mice (Figure 1G).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text with statistical significance and supported by Figure 1E,G showing the data.

claim: The numbers of EYFP+ pre-myelinating OLs (pre-OLs, NG2- CC1-) and EYFP+ OPCs (NG2+) were not significantly affected in Tsc1 cKO mice, except for cortical pre-OLs that were increased.
source: In contrast, the numbers of EYFP+ pre-myelinating OLs (pre-OLs, NG2- CC1-) and EYFP+ OPCs (NG2+) were not significantly affected, except for cortical pre-OLs that were increased in the Tsc1 cKO (Figure 1H,I).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1H,I showing the data.

claim: The proportion of OPCs and pre-OLs became significantly larger, whereas that of mature OLs was markedly reduced in both the CC and CTX of Tsc1 cKO mice.
source: Consequently, despite no or only a small increase in labeled OPCs and pre-OLs, the composition of EYFP-labeled cells changed to a state where the proportion of OPCs and pre-OLs became significantly larger, whereas that of mature OLs was markedly reduced in both the CC and CTX (Figure 1J).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1J showing the data.

claim: The percentage of Ki67+ cells among cortical EYFP+ OPCs was higher in Tsc1 cKO mice than in control.
source: The percentage of Ki67+ cells among cortical EYFP+ OPCs was even higher in the cKO mice than in control (Figure 1L).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1L showing the data.

claim: There was a slight reduction in total OPCs in the CTX of Tsc1 cKO mice.
source: Nonetheless, there was a slight reduction in total OPCs in the CTX of the cKO mice (Figure 1M).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1M showing the data.

claim: The marked decrease of new OLs in Tsc1 cKO mice is not due to OPC proliferation defects.
source: These observations indicate that the marked decrease of new OLs in the cKO mice is not due to OPC proliferation defects.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the text based on the proliferation data.

claim: The levels of MBP expression were reduced in the CTX of Tsc1 cKO mice at P20+21.
source: Consistent with the impaired OL accumulation, the levels of MBP expression were also reduced in the CTX of Tsc1 cKO mice (P20 +21) (Figure 1N,O).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1N,O showing the western blot data.

claim: Pre-OL-to-OL lineage progression is arrested and/or newly born OLs undergo premature cell death in Tsc1 cKO mice.
source: These results raise two possibilities that are not mutually exclusive: Pre-OL-to-OL lineage progression is arrested, and/or newly born OLs undergo premature cell death.
evidence: This is stated as a speculative interpretation of the results.

claim: A complete inactivation of TSC1 (or consequent mTORC1 hyperactivation) is detrimental to OLs.
source: Along with others' results on OL lineage cKO of Tsc1 or Tsc2 (Carson et al., 2015; Jiang et al., 2016; Lebrun-Julien et al., 2014), our results further support the idea that a complete inactivation of TSC1 (or consequent mTORC1 hyperactivation) is detrimental to OLs, and thus would not benefit OL development or remyelination.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the text based on the current study's data and previous literature with citations.

claim: Pten deletion increased pS6 levels in EYFP+ cells in the CC.
source: Similar to Tsc1 cKO, Pten deletion increased pS6 levels in EYFP+ cells in the CC (Figure 2B,C), indicating that PTEN was inactivated, and as a consequence, mTORC1 activity was significantly enhanced.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2B,C showing the data.

claim: The increase in pS6 levels indicates that PTEN was inactivated and mTORC1 activity was significantly enhanced.
source: Similar to Tsc1 cKO, Pten deletion increased pS6 levels in EYFP+ cells in the CC (Figure 2B,C), indicating that PTEN was inactivated, and as a consequence, mTORC1 activity was significantly enhanced.
evidence: This interpretation is stated in the text and supported by the data in Figure 2B,C.

claim: The number of EYFP+ cells increased for most of the observed brain areas, including the CC and CTX, in Pten cKO mice.
source: However, in contrast to Tsc1 cKO, the number of EYFP+ cells increased for most of the observed brain areas, including the CC and CTX (Figure 2D,E).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2D,E showing the data.

claim: There were significant increases in EYFP+CC1+ cells in the CTX of Pten cKO mice for both age-windows (P20~P41 and P45~P75).
source: The fate analysis of EYFP-labeled OPCs with co-immunostaining of cell stage markers (Figure 2D) revealed that there were significant increases in EYFP+CC1+ cells in the CTX of Pten cKO mice for both age-windows (p=0.0002 for P20 ~P41; p=0.0037 for P45 ~P75) (Figure 2F).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text with statistical significance and supported by Figure 2D,F showing the data.

claim: New OL generation was higher in the CC of P45+30 Pten cKO mice than the age-matched control.
source: The new OL generation was also higher in the CC of P45 +30 Pten cKO mice than the age-matched control (p=0.0006) (Figure 2F).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text with statistical significance and supported by Figure 2F showing the data.

claim: The percentage of mature OLs among EYFP-labeled OL lineage cells increased in both the CC (for P45+30) and CTX in Pten cKO mice.
source: Consequently, the percentage of mature OLs among EYFP-labeled OL lineage cells increased in both the CC (for P45 +30) and CTX (Figure 2H).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2H showing the data.

claim: PTEN inactivation in OPCs promotes new OL development, even in the mature brain.
source: These results strongly suggest that PTEN inactivation in OPCs promotes new OL development, even in the mature brain.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the text based on the experimental findings.

claim: There were marked increases in BrdU+ cells in the Pten cKO brain at P20+21.
source: We observed that there were marked increases in BrdU+ cells in the Pten cKO brain (P20 +21) (Figure 2I left).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2I showing the data.

claim: Most BrdU+ cells were NG2+ OPCs for both age windows in Pten cKO mice.
source: Confocal imaging further confirmed that most BrdU+ cells were NG2+ OPCs for both age windows (Figure 2I,J).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2I,J showing the data.

claim: The characteristic tiled distribution of OPCs was disrupted by OPC-specific Pten cKO.
source: It was also noted that the characteristic tiled distribution of OPCs (Hughes et al., 2013) was disrupted by OPC-specific Pten cKO (Figure 2K).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text with a citation and supported by Figure 2K showing the data.

claim: Despite the increase of OPC proliferation, the density of total OPCs was not altered in Pten cKO mice.
source: However, despite the increase of OPC proliferation, the density of total OPCs was not altered (Figure 2L).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2L showing the data.

claim: The increased OPC proliferation directly contributes to additional OL differentiation and/or is a homeostatic regenerative response to the OPC reduction due to enhanced OPC-to-OL conversion in Pten cKO mice.
source: These observations suggest that the increased OPC proliferation directly contributes to additional OL differentiation and/or that it is a homeostatic regenerative response to the OPC reduction due to enhanced OPC-to-OL conversion in Pten cKO mice.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the text based on the proliferation and differentiation data.

claim: After OPC-specific Pten ablation starting at P45, new OL accumulation was enhanced by about four-fold in the SC GM in 30 days.
source: In particular, after OPC-specific Pten ablation starting at P45, new OL accumulation was enhanced by about four-fold in the SC GM in 30 days (p=0.0001) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text with statistical significance and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1C showing the data.

claim: OPC-specific PTEN inactivation effectively promotes new OL development throughout the CNS.
source: These results further suggest that OPC-specific PTEN inactivation effectively promotes new OL development throughout the CNS.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the text based on the experimental findings in multiple CNS regions.

claim: At P30, there were increases in both EGFP+ OLs and Olig2+CC1+ OLs in the CTX of Pten cKO mice.
source: At P30, there were increases in both EGFP+ OLs (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,C) and Olig2+CC1+ OLs (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D,E) in the CTX of Pten cKO mice.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 1B-E showing the data.

claim: Pten cKO mice exhibited even greater accumulation of EYFP+ OLs in both the CC and CTX at P20+70 compared to P20+21.
source: These cKO mice exhibited even greater accumulation of EYFP+ OLs in both the CC and CTX (a seven-fold increase of OL at P20 +70 vs. a two-fold increase at P20 +21) (Figures 3B–D and and 2F).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figures 3B-D and 2F showing the data.

claim: Total CC1+ OLs increased in Pten cKO mice at P20+70.
source: Due to the greater new OL addition, total CC1+ OLs also increased (Figure 3E).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3E showing the data.

claim: EYFP+NG2+ OPCs were significantly reduced in the CC but not in the CTX of Pten cKO mice at P20+70.
source: Interestingly, EYFP+NG2+ OPCs were significantly reduced in the CC (p=0.0004), but not in the CTX of Pten cKO mice (P20 +70) (Figure 3F).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text with statistical significance and supported by Figure 3F showing the data.

claim: The percentages of mature OLs among EYFP-labeled cells were increased in both the CC and CTX, whereas those of labeled OPCs were highly reduced at P20+70 in Pten cKO mice.
source: Due to the marked EYFP+ OL accumulation, the percentages of mature OLs among EYFP-labeled cells were increased, both in the CC and CTX, whereas those of labeled OPCs were highly reduced (Figure 3G).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3G showing the data.

claim: PTEN-deficient (EYFP+) OPCs in the CC may have undergone OL differentiation more rapidly than their own cell division, and thus EYFP-labeled OPCs markedly decreased at P20+70.
source: It is likely that the PTEN-deficient (EYFP+) OPCs in the CC may have undergone OL differentiation more rapidly than their own cell division, and thus EYFP-labeled OPCs markedly decreased at P20 +70.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the text based on the observed data.

claim: At P20+70, EYFP-Olig2+NG2+ OPCs were predominant in the CC of Pten cKO mice.
source: Indeed, at P20 +70, EYFP-Olig2+NG2+ OPCs were predominant in the CC of Pten cKO mice (Figure 3H), and thus, the density of total OPCs was not altered (Figure 3I).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3H,I showing the data.

claim: The density of total OPCs was not altered at P20+70 in Pten cKO mice.
source: Indeed, at P20 +70, EYFP-Olig2+NG2+ OPCs were predominant in the CC of Pten cKO mice (Figure 3H), and thus, the density of total OPCs was not altered (Figure 3I).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3I showing the data.

claim: OPCs continuously proliferate at higher rates in the CTX of Pten cKO mice.
source: BrdU administration (50 mg/kg per injection, a total of 10 injections between P80 and P84) and cell proliferation analyses revealed that OPCs continuously proliferate at higher rates in the CTX of Pten cKO (Figure 3J,K), and yet without changes in total OPC number (Figure 3I).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3J,K showing the data.

claim: Some of the BrdU-laden OPCs appeared to have become pre-OLs or OLs (EYFP+NG2-) during the last week before sampling.
source: Some of the BrdU-laden OPCs appeared to have become pre-OLs or OLs (EYFP+NG2-) during the last week before sampling (Figure 3K right).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3K showing the data.

claim: PTEN regulates OPC differentiation not only in early postnatal life but also at later adult ages.
source: These results further confirm that PTEN regulates OPC differentiation, not only in early postnatal life but also at later adult ages.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the text based on the experimental findings at different ages.

claim: The enhanced OL differentiation by PTEN inactivation is not a transient event.
source: These also suggest that the enhanced OL differentiation by PTEN inactivation is not a transient event, and that the newly generated OLs from PTEN-deficient OPCs survive long.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the text based on the long-term fate mapping data.

claim: The newly generated OLs from PTEN-deficient OPCs survive long.
source: These also suggest that the enhanced OL differentiation by PTEN inactivation is not a transient event, and that the newly generated OLs from PTEN-deficient OPCs survive long.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the text based on the long-term fate mapping data.

claim: The enhanced proliferation in Pten cKO mice is tightly controlled to maintain OPC homeostasis.
source: Although OPC proliferation remained promoted in the CTX, it appears that this enhanced proliferation is tightly controlled to maintain OPC homeostasis.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the text based on the observation that total OPC numbers remain constant despite increased proliferation.

claim: Levels of PLP, MOG, and CNP were significantly increased in the CTX of Pten cKO mice at P75.
source: Even though Pten might have been deleted from only subsets of young OPCs by this Cre activation protocol, levels of PLP, MOG, and CNP were significantly increased in the CTX of Pten cKO mice at P75 (Figure 4B,C).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4B,C showing the western blot data.

claim: The g-ratios of callosal axon fibers were significantly lowered in Pten cKO mice at P13+17.
source: Moreover, electron microscopic (EM) analyses revealed that the g-ratios (the ratio between the inner and the outer diameters of the myelin sheath) of callosal axon fibers were significantly lowered in the Pten cKO mice (P13 +17) (p=0.038) (Figure 4D–F).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text with statistical significance and supported by Figure 4D-F showing the EM data.

claim: There was a marked increase in the number of myelinated axons in OPC-specific Pten cKO mice.
source: More importantly, there was a marked increase in the number of myelinated axons (p=0.033) (Figure 4G), suggesting that the increased number of new OLs myelinate more axons in OPC-specific Pten cKO mice.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text with statistical significance and supported by Figure 4G showing the data.

claim: The increased number of new OLs myelinate more axons in OPC-specific Pten cKO mice.
source: More importantly, there was a marked increase in the number of myelinated axons (p=0.033) (Figure 4G), suggesting that the increased number of new OLs myelinate more axons in OPC-specific Pten cKO mice.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the text based on the myelination data in Figure 4G.

claim: EGFP+ cells exhibited more rapid morphological changes in Pten cKO mice.
source: In a few weeks after 4HT administration (at P25), EGFP+ cells exhibited more rapid morphological changes in the Pten cKO mice, and the EGFP+ OPC progeny cells formed more thin processes along axonal tracts (Figure 4H,I).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4H,I showing the data.

claim: At P25+20, discrete stellate-shaped OPC morphology was no longer seen in the CC of Pten cKO mice.
source: Consequently, at P25 +20, discrete stellate-shaped OPC morphology was no longer seen in the CC of cKO mice (Figure 4H).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4H showing the data.

claim: The percentage of newly formed myelinated axons increased by about 2.5-fold in the CC of Pten cKO mice at P20+21.
source: The immuno-EM analysis revealed that the percentage of newly formed myelinated axons increased by about 2.5-fold in the CC of the Pten cKO mice (p=0.0179) (Figure 4K).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text with statistical significance and supported by Figure 4K showing the immuno-EM data.

claim: PTEN inactivation in OPCs facilitates and enhances new myelination.
source: These results suggest that PTEN inactivation in OPCs facilitates and enhances new myelination.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the text based on the myelination data.

claim: In Mog-iCre; R26-EYFP; ±Ptenf/f mice at P41, EYFP was expressed only in CC1+ OLs.
source: In Mog-iCre; R26-EYFP; ±Ptenf/f mice (P41), EYFP was expressed only in CC1+ OLs (Figure 5A), suggesting that the Cre activity is highly specific to OLs.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5A showing the data.

claim: The Cre activity in Mog-iCre mice is highly specific to OLs.
source: In Mog-iCre; R26-EYFP; ±Ptenf/f mice (P41), EYFP was expressed only in CC1+ OLs (Figure 5A), suggesting that the Cre activity is highly specific to OLs.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the text based on the EYFP expression pattern in Figure 5A.

claim: The numbers of EYFP+ OLs and NG2+ OPCs were not changed by Mog-iCre-based Pten cKO for both the brain and the spinal cord.
source: The numbers of EYFP+ OLs and NG2+ OPCs were not changed by the Mog-iCre-based Pten cKO for both the brain and the spinal cord (Figure 5B,C).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5B,C showing the data.

claim: Myelin sheaths were thickened in OL-specific Pten cKO mice at P34.
source: Moreover, EM analysis of R26-EYFP; Ptenf/f; ±Mog-iCre (P34) mice revealed that myelin sheaths were thickened (Figure 5D–F), but the percentage of myelinated axons did not increase in the cKO mice (Figure 5G).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5D-F showing the EM data.

claim: The percentage of myelinated axons did not increase in OL-specific Pten cKO mice.
source: Moreover, EM analysis of R26-EYFP; Ptenf/f; ±Mog-iCre (P34) mice revealed that myelin sheaths were thickened (Figure 5D–F), but the percentage of myelinated axons did not increase in the cKO mice (Figure 5G).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5G showing the data.

claim: The enhanced oligodendrogenesis in Pdgfra-CreER; Ptenf/f mice is due to OPC-specific targeting of Pten.
source: These results are in accordance with the earlier reports (Flores et al., 2008; Goebbels et al., 2010), and together they support the notion that the enhanced oligodendrogenesis (promoted OL generation and increase in myelinated axons) in Pdgfra-CreER; Ptenf/f mice is due to OPC-specific targeting of Pten, thus suggesting differential cell-stage-specific roles of PTEN.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the text based on the comparison of OPC-specific and OL-specific Pten deletion results, with supporting citations.

claim: PTEN has differential cell-stage-specific roles.
source: These results are in accordance with the earlier reports (Flores et al., 2008; Goebbels et al., 2010), and together they support the notion that the enhanced oligodendrogenesis (promoted OL generation and increase in myelinated axons) in Pdgfra-CreER; Ptenf/f mice is due to OPC-specific targeting of Pten, thus suggesting differential cell-stage-specific roles of PTEN.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the text based on the differential effects of OPC-specific vs OL-specific Pten deletion.

claim: More EYFP+CC1+ OLs accumulated in the CC of Pten cKO mice two weeks after LPC injection.
source: Two weeks after LPC, we observed that more EYFP+CC1+ OLs accumulated in the CC of Pten cKO mice (p=0.01) (Figure 6C–E), while EYFP-labeled OPCs were unchanged (Figure 6F).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text with statistical significance and supported by Figure 6C-E showing the data.

claim: EYFP-labeled OPCs were unchanged two weeks after LPC injection in Pten cKO mice.
source: Two weeks after LPC, we observed that more EYFP+CC1+ OLs accumulated in the CC of Pten cKO mice (p=0.01) (Figure 6C–E), while EYFP-labeled OPCs were unchanged (Figure 6F).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 6F showing the data.
